mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 3 months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a flattening industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND INDPRO m/m change < 0 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below the historical mean at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero or are positive in more than 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months indicates a supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above the median or are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% for two consecutive months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which can depress risk asset valuations due to lower growth expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 100 (i.e., <1% YoY) for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero or are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average by >10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above the median or are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 per month for three consecutive months, accompanied by a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS m/m > 100,000 for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE m/m change within ±0.1% each month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero or are negative in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) of more than 2% for four consecutive months indicates households are drawing down savings to finance consumption, which temporarily supports demand but ultimately signals a reduction in future fiscal buffers, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below the median or are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
